title: On the Collapse of Generative Paths: A Criterion and Correction for Diffusion Steering
claim: Constant-exponent composition is biased or collapses when its validity criterion goes negative; adaptive exponents keep it positive and recover ground truth.
layout: 4 panels in 2x2 grid; three 3D sample-path panels plus criterion plot
description: A 2x2 grid. Panels (a), (b) and (c) each show a pseudo-3D plot of blue sample clouds and black trajectories evolving along a time axis from p0, a Gaussian blob on the left, to p1, a checkerboard on the right. Each has a small inset of the final 2D samples. (a) is Heuristic Steering (NR), with a red dashed ellipse on stray artifacts near the end. (b) is FKC, where trajectories funnel into a narrow stream. A large red dashed ellipse marks the collapse, and the inset shows only a couple of clusters. (c) is ACE (Ours), with a clean checkerboard result. (d) plots the criterion C(t) against time for constant exponents (blue, dropping below zero) and adaptive exponents (orange, staying positive). Callouts link the curves to the panels, and a ground-truth checkerboard inset sits below the plot.
caption: Marginal Path Collapse breaks heterogeneous composition. We synthesize a 2D Checkerboard via three heterogeneous experts: two 1D priors and a 2D constraint. (a) Standard Steering (NR) is biased, failing to filter low-density artifacts. (b) Feynman–Kac Corrector (FKC) fails catastrophically because the path existence criterion C(t) becomes negative (Collapse). (c) ACE (Ours) dynamically adjusts exponents to ensure C(t) > 0, recovering the ground truth. (d) Validity Analysis: ACE maintains positive criterion values while baselines dive into invalid regions.
abstract: Inference-time steering adapts pretrained diffusion and flow models to new tasks without retraining, often utilizing ratio-of-densities constructions that reweight time-indexed marginals with fixed exponents. We identify Marginal Path Collapse, a failure mode in which the intermediate density defined by such compositions becomes non-normalizable despite valid endpoints. This collapse can arise when composing heterogeneous experts trained with mismatched noise schedules (and/or negative exponents / partial supports). To address this, we provide (i) a sharp sufficient Path Existence Criterion that characterizes when the composed intermediate densities are mathematically well-defined, and (ii) Adaptive Path Correction with Exponents (ACE), which generalizes Feynman-Kac steering to support time-varying exponents. Our analysis reveals that ACE controls the quantile radius of the intermediate distributions, providing a theoretical mechanism for path stabilization observed in experiments. On flexible-pose scaffold decoration, a drug design task composed of de-novo, conformer, and protein-conditioned experts, ACE prevents collapse and significantly outperforms constant-exponent baselines. Furthermore, ACE improves attribute success rates in compositional image generation, establishing it as a general framework for compositional sampling.
